coverage: Somali seasonal components, historical Davidson winter reach, Sri Lanka Monsoon Current summer/winter regional drawings, and one Indian SECC winter surface reach. Incomplete annual coverage; not observed monthly fields or occupied footprints.

frames.time_convention: Northeast winter monsoon convention; not a simultaneous dated observation or an annual-average route.
frames.layer: Surface/upper-layer seasonal coastal reference geography; the source describes a shallow winter equatorial current, but no fixed-depth velocity axis is reconstructed.
frames.source_locator: Section 4.2.1, printed pages 48-49 (PDF indices 47-48): southward surface flow reaches EACC confluence at 2-4 S; winter coastal divergence near 6-8 N. Section 4.2.2 distinguishes modeled coastal continuation and northern countercurrent.

frames.time_convention: June-July monsoon-onset two-gyre convention. Does not assume rare late-summer gyre coalescence or persistent whole-coast continuity.
frames.layer: Upper-layer southern seasonal coastal geography; no fixed-depth or velocity-derived axis.
frames.source_locator: Section 4.1.1, printed page 38 (PDF index 37): June-July cross-equatorial limb departs the coast south of 4 N, partitions into offshore outflow/recirculation and has little exchange with Great Whirl. Printed pages 41-43 discuss non-universal gyre coalescence.

frames.width_scope_note: Approximate 64 km is historical California-Oregon regional context; it is not applied uniformly to the editorial route or used as an occupied footprint.
frames.time_convention: October-March California-Oregon regional seasonal description in the February 1978 report; strongest flow described in January. Historical summary, not a dated trajectory, current-year observation or modern monthly climatology.
frames.layer: Seasonal northward surface-current regional context; not the separately described California Undercurrent below 200 m or a reconstructed velocity axis.
frames.source_locator: Appendix II section II.1, printed II-1 to II-2 / PDF pages 12-13: northward seasonal surface strip along California and Oregon from October to March; Vancouver Island penetration is conditional.

frames.time_convention: Source boreal winter December-March convention; Gauss-Markov seasonal climatology using 1993-2018 drifter context. Not a dated trajectory or complete annual route series.

frames.source_locator: Sections 2.1-2.2: drifter support, 1993-2018 selection, fitted seasonal fields and December-March winter. Section 3 seasonal discussion after Figures 5-6: eastward SECC reaches about 90 E before recirculating into SEC; Figure 13 caption.

comparability.reason: Winter coastal branch and June-July southern limb have different source-defined spatial scopes; their nominal lengths or scenario bounds do not define annual whole-current extrema.

Only historical October-March California-Oregon reference geography and width context are available. April-September width and seasonal route geometry remain unknown; no modern annual cycle, seasonal extrema or uniform width footprint established.

Two source-defined seasonal phases with editorial 77–83 E regional drawings. Their different latitude choices and scenario envelopes are not observed annual length minima/maxima. March–May and October geometry and all seasonal widths remain unresolved; month labels do not provide monthly velocity fields.
